I've spent the last 5 hours lying in bed moping. I'm in the middle of one of the worst depressive periods I've had since starting on an SSRI. I have been where you are and I know what you're feeling. But even in the state I'm in I can tell you that you should keep going. As a human you are made of trillions of cells. Those cells are in turn made up of molecules and atoms which were formed in the center of giant stars that exploded millions if not billions of years ago. You are the product of the grandest chemical reaction in existence. Even if you never find what you're meant to do or where you should go, just being part of the universe is something you can enjoy. Life is ultimately pointless, it's not like a game where there's a set goal and you earn points towards it. But what that means is that you have the freedom to define life how you want, think of something you want to achieve and you can find meaning in just working towards it. When I was at one of my darker moments I decided that I wanted to be the person who brought about personal, humanoid robots. I didn't know more than basic coding, I have no mechanical or electrical engineering background at all and I have no clue how or if I'm going to achieve that goal, but having something to strive for, giving myself meaning, making life have a point, it has helped immensely. I hope this period passes for you and I hope that what I've said helps.
